method: node tools/globals.js --scan base-fold, then classify by signal per docs/globals-step2-plan.md

globals.evidence: Every user loads it then computes 351*i via lea/lea/shl/sub. Array base derived as 0xcde6e, since the fields at 0xcde76, 0xcde7c, 0xcde89 and 0xcdf6b sit at offsets 8, 14, 27 and 253 within one 351-byte record. Structured recovered from 0xef248 confirms sizeof(struct S) == 351.

recovered_routines.diff: 12 bytes across four disp32 relocation fields: the global at 1..3, and the struct field at 22..24, 28..30, 40..42. No other byte differs in 49.
recovered_routines.behaviour: Adds n to a per-record counter and clamps it at 9999, which is 0x270f. Reads like a money or score cap.

globals.evidence: Always [reg*4+0xce408]: mov/cmp/sub/add with a scaled index. Adjacent to 0xce488, which is the same table one field on.
Same four users as 0xce408 and the same [reg*4+addr] form, 0x80 bytes higher. A pair of parallel per-id tables.
All three users contain cli/out/in. 0xfec70 has pushfw, cli, in al,dx, out dx,al, popfw around the access. Not a game global.
Same three hardware routines as 0xdf0c7, used as a latch byte cleared to 0 between port writes.
mov dword [0xd6e60],0x30 initialises it; compared against 0 and decremented. No index chain, so it is a counter or mode word.

recovered_routines.diff: bytes 2..5 only, the displacement of mov dword [0xd6e60],0x30

_note: Counts corrected: 122 distinct globals, not 118. tools/globals_od.js found that the ndisasm classifier missed [eax+edx+0x392c8] forms (base+index with an implicit scale of 1, which ndisasm prints with no *1). Four globals at 0x392c8..0x392d4 were invisible. See docs/objdump-crosscheck.md.
